162: [edit] One must sit within the air of the sukkah [i.e. directly under the space of the s’chach]. One who sleeps under a bed in the sukkah that is ten handbreaths high has not fulfilled the obligation.
[edit] One who sleeps under a slanting canopy in a sukkah that is not ten handbreaths tall or that has no handbreath-wide roof has fulfilled the obligation.

[edit] It is forbidden to hang a sheet over the four bedposts to sleep under it, even if they are not ten [handbreaths] tall. However, if one ascends from the head and two from the foot [of the bed] and beams (meaning long pieces of wood like handle of a pike) are placed between them, it is permitted to spread sheets over it and sleep under because it has no handbreath-wide roof above. This applies when they are not higher than ten handbreaths. There are those who declare this valid even if it is greater than ten tefachim.

[edit] If one hangs fabric under the schach for ornamentation and is within four tefachim of the roof, it is valid. If it is farther than four tefachim from the roof, it is invalid. And if it is not for ornamentation, even if it is within four tefachim, it is invalid. (One should be careful to only hang decorations in the sukkah within four handbreaths of the [roof of the] sukkah (Mahari"l).)
